revision.scope: All 2,006 retained character associations are present in both Unihan 17.0 variant properties after inclusive range expansion. A targeted audit of 42 previously unverified lexical notes is complete: 38 supported and 4 supported with spelling/literary qualifications. The full mainland 2013 standard is not yet checked pair-by-pair. These mappings are not unconditional sentence conversions. Catalogue script-label conflict count (zero) is attributed to an independent audit, not reproduced here.
rules: Entries are possible character associations, not unconditional substitutions.
Meaning, reading, lexical context and region determine the correct traditional form.
Original forms can remain unchanged in traditional writing, even if not explicitly listed as self mappings.
Do not infer historical origin from a simplified/traditional relation.
Never turn component-only correspondences into standalone-character replacements.

classificationGuide.context_dependent_not_error: Retain pair but convert only in the applicable word, reading or meaning.
classificationGuide.orthographic_variant: Listed under the 2013 standard’s variant-character column, not its traditional-character column.
classificationGuide.regional_variant: Established regional traditional written form; may differ from 2013 mainland traditional-character column.
classificationGuide.traditional: Association classified under the 2013 mainland traditional-character column, when standardRelation2013=traditional.
classificationGuide.attested_alternate_form: Unihan attests the form relationship; regional usage and/or normative category is not fully verified for this pair.
classificationGuide.lexicalExampleEvidenceStatus: not_individually_verified_against_lexical_source means the generic technical citation does not validate the exact example.

standardRelation2013Guide.traditional: Listed in the traditional-character column of the 2013 mainland standard (not necessarily a context-free mapping).
standardRelation2013Guide.orthographic_variant: Listed in the orthographic-variant column of the 2013 mainland standard.
standardRelation2013Guide.regional_traditional_form: Traditional written form evidenced in other regional conventions; not listed as the traditional glyph by the 2013 mainland appendix.
standardRelation2013Guide.requires_review: Not yet checked against the printed 2013 mainland appendix entry. Do not infer that traditional script usage implies traditional-column status.

revision.verificationUpdate: Pinned Unihan 17.0 range-aware validation: 2,006/2,006 forward matches, 2,006/2,006 reverse matches, and zero forward-only exceptions. The earlier nine false negatives resulted from treating compact code-point-range keys (for example 9EBC..9EBD) as single-code-point entries. The independent catalogue audit reports zero script-label conflicts. Full 2013 mainland-standard certification remains incomplete.

徵.usageCaveat: The choice is lexical/context-dependent; do not treat 征→徵 as unconditional.

準.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

韆.explanation: 韆 is the differentiated final character in the traditional word for a swing, 鞦韆; 千 meaning one thousand remains 千.
韆.example: 秋千 → 鞦韆; 一千 → 一千
韆.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

蔔.explanation: 蔔 represents the radish-related use of 卜 (as in 蘿蔔); 卜 meaning divination remains 卜.
蔔.example: 萝卜 → 蘿蔔; 占卜 → 占卜
蔔.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

閤.explanation: Traditional 閤 (hé) occurs in certain whole-family/whole-household expressions (e.g. 閤家, 閤府) and in the hé sense “close” (e.g. 閤眼). This should not be confused with the distinct gé reading associated with small-gate/inner-chamber senses. Most uses of 合 (hé, join/combine) remain 合.
閤.unchangedSense: join/combine, as in 合作 (hézuò); do not generally replace 合 with 閤.
閤.usageCaveat: Only specific traditional lexical contexts use 閤; the historical small-gate explanation concerns a different reading and is not justification for the hé phrase conversion.
閤.evidenceScope: 合家 and 合府 checked directly in OpenCC 1.4.2 STPhrases; hé meaning also checked against the Taiwan MOE dictionary. 合作 is an unchanged illustration, not claimed as an explicit OpenCC phrase-table entry.
閤.example: 合家 → 閤家; 合府 → 閤府; 合作 → 合作

sources.basis: STPhrases explicit 合家/合府 mappings
Taiwan MOE: 閤 hé = close, whole/all; distinguishes gé reading
2013 mainland appendix 合 → 閤 lists contextual traditional counterpart

摺.explanation: 摺 is used for folding/pleating in some traditional writing; 折 meaning break, discount, etc., remains 折.
摺.example: 折叠 → 摺疊 (regional usage); 折断 → 折斷
摺.usageCaveat: Traditional usage varies regionally; 折疊 is also seen.
摺.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

樸.explanation: 樸 represents simple/plain/unadorned; 朴 may remain unchanged in surnames and other distinct lexical senses.
樸.example: 朴素 → 樸素; 姓朴 → 姓朴
樸.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

硃.explanation: 硃 distinguishes vermilion/cinnabar-related uses; 朱 remains in ordinary red and surname senses.
硃.example: 朱砂 → 硃砂 (differentiated spelling); 朱先生 → 朱先生
硃.usageCaveat: 朱砂 also occurs in traditional writing.
硃.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

麯.explanation: 麯 is used for fermentation starter/yeast; 曲 remains for bends, melodies, and musical compositions.
麯.example: 酒曲 → 酒麯; 曲线 → 曲線
麯.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

捲.explanation: 捲 is used when rolling, winding or curling; 卷 remains for a scroll, volume, paper or examination.
捲.example: 卷起 → 捲起; 试卷 → 試卷
捲.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

鞦.explanation: 鞦 is used in the traditional spelling 鞦韆 (swing); 秋 meaning autumn remains 秋.
鞦.example: 秋千 → 鞦韆; 秋天 → 秋天
鞦.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

衊.explanation: 衊 is used for smearing or defaming, as in 誣衊; 蔑 remains in the sense of despising.
衊.example: 诬蔑 → 誣衊; 轻蔑 → 輕蔑
衊.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

緻.explanation: 緻 is used for fine, delicate or intricate texture; 致 remains for cause, send, or convey.
緻.example: 精致 → 精緻; 致谢 → 致謝
緻.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

捨.explanation: 捨 is used when giving up, abandoning or relinquishing; 舍 remains for dwelling, dormitory and related senses.
捨.example: 舍弃 → 捨棄; 宿舍 → 宿舍
捨.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

願.explanation: 願 is the normal traditional form for wishing, desiring or being willing; 愿 may survive as a distinct literary character meaning honest/cautious.
願.usageCaveat: The 2013 table lists 願 as the traditional counterpart; uncommon inherited use of 愿 should not be automatically converted.
願.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

禦.explanation: 禦 is used for defending, resisting, or warding off; 御 remains for imperial and certain control senses.
禦.example: 抵御 → 抵禦; 御用 → 御用
禦.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

誌.explanation: The 2013 standard lists 誌 as an orthographic variant of 志, not in its traditional-character column. In differentiated traditional writing 誌 is common for recording and periodical/magazine senses.
誌.example: 杂志 → 雜誌; 志向 → 志向
誌.usageCaveat: Keep as a searchable variant relationship, not a formally listed 2013 traditional-character pair.
誌.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

藉.explanation: Only some historical/lexical uses of 藉 correspond to simplified 借. The 2013 standard explicitly requires 藉 to remain 藉 when pronounced jí or for consolation/cushioning senses, including 狼藉 and 枕藉.
藉.example: 借钱 → 借錢 (not 藉錢); 狼藉 → 狼藉; 枕藉 → 枕藉
藉.unchangedSense: 借 meaning borrow; 藉 pronounced jí or consolation/cushioning
藉.usageCaveat: Do not infer 借→藉 for ordinary borrowing, or replace restricted uses of 藉 with 借.
藉.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

剋.explanation: The standard lists the relationship but explicitly does not simplify 剋 pronounced kēi when it means scolding or hitting. 克 also remains unchanged in ordinary words meaning overcome/gram.
剋.example: 克服 → 克服; 剋人 (kēi, scold/hit) remains 剋
剋.unchangedSense: 克服 and inherited uses of 克; 剋 read kēi for scolding/hitting
剋.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

鼕.explanation: 鼕 represents a drum-like onomatopoeic sound in differentiated traditional usage, not the season winter. 冬 remains unchanged for winter.
鼕.example: 冬天 → 冬天; 鼕鼕 (drum-sound word)
鼕.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

纔.explanation: 纔 is a differentiated traditional form for the adverb meaning just/only/recently; 才 meaning talent or ability remains 才.
纔.example: 天才 → 天才; 刚才 → 剛纔 (differentiated spelling)
纔.usageCaveat: Traditional practice can also use 才 in adverbial contexts.
纔.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

麽.explanation: The mainland 2013 appendix lists 麽 as the traditional counterpart for 么 in the me particle sense.
麽.unchangedSense: Independent use of 么 is not an instruction to replace every occurrence.
麽.usageCaveat: Not an unconditional replacement for 么 with other readings.
麽.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

麼.explanation: 麼 is an established regional traditional spelling for the me particle, especially in Taiwan/Hong Kong conventions. It is not the traditional-character glyph printed in the 2013 mainland appendix, which uses 麽.
麼.example: 什么 → 什麼 (regional traditional spelling)
麼.usageCaveat: Retained from Unihan; not listed as the traditional glyph for 么 in the 2013 mainland appendix.
麼.evidenceScope: All examples in this note were individually reviewed against cited pinned OpenCC phrase records or identified supplementary sources. This does not establish unconditional character conversion, all regional spelling choices or full mainland-2013 certification.

lexicalEvidence.methodology: Exact version-pinned phrase records, with independently identified dictionary, composed-example or literary evidence where needed; no native OpenCC execution was performed.

涼.explanation: The 2013 mainland standard places 涼 in the orthographic-variant column for 凉 rather than in its traditional-character column. The glyph 涼 remains common in traditional-script regions.
涼.example: 凉快 → 涼快 (traditional regional writing)
涼.usageCaveat: Retain the association but do not label it an official 2013 mainland traditional-character pair.
涼.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

決.explanation: The 2013 mainland appendix places 決 in the orthographic-variant column for 决. 決 is a normal traditional-writing form in regions using traditional characters.
決.example: 决定 → 決定 (juédìng, regional traditional spelling)
決.usageCaveat: Do not label 決 as a traditional-column form under the 2013 mainland classification.
決.evidenceScope: 2013 Appendix 1 row 0523 verified; regional spellings can use a glyph that the mainland appendix classifies as an orthographic variant.

產.explanation: Common traditional-script shape for “produce; property; products”; the 2013 mainland appendix prints 産 instead of 產 in its traditional column.
產.usageCaveat: A regional character-form distinction, not a separate sense of “produce”.
產.evidenceScope: 2013 appendix row directly checked for classification; lexical equivalence is not a context-free replacement.

産.explanation: Traditional-column form printed for 产 in the 2013 mainland standard; visually differs from the more familiar 產 used in some traditional-writing regions.
産.evidenceScope: 2013 appendix row directly checked for classification; lexical equivalence is not a context-free replacement.

眾.explanation: Graphical variant for “crowd; many”; the 2013 mainland appendix places 眾 in the orthographic-variant column (the common form in many traditional regions).
眾.evidenceScope: 2013 appendix row directly checked for classification; lexical equivalence is not a context-free replacement.

衆.explanation: Traditional-column form of 众 in the 2013 mainland appendix; same ordinary “crowd; many” meaning as 眾.
衆.evidenceScope: 2013 appendix row directly checked for classification; lexical equivalence is not a context-free replacement.

別.explanation: Traditional rendering for the ordinary “other; different; separate” senses.
別.evidenceScope: OpenCC 1.4.2 explicitly maps 别人 to 別人; other lexical contexts require independent checking.

Both 飢餓 and 饑餓 are attested. Separate the two dictionary attestations from the OpenCC phrase policy, which records 飢餓; do not describe the slash as two OpenCC outputs or an exclusive Taiwan/Hong Kong rule.
